claims.text: Laser-assisted fabrication under a controlled atmosphere can overcome phase separation and void formation in W–Cu composites.
Rapid laser melting of the Cu phase enhances interfacial bonding between Cu and W.
Enhanced W–Cu interfacial bonding improves thermal transport.
Enhanced W–Cu interfacial bonding improves mechanical durability under fusion-reactor irradiation.
An inert or reducing atmosphere can avoid oxidation during laser-assisted W–Cu fabrication.
Laser parameters can be optimized to melt Cu fully without causing significant Cu vaporization.
Rapid localized melting and resolidification of Cu promotes wetting and bonding with W.
Rapid localized Cu melting and resolidification produces a more uniform W–Cu microstructure.
Rapid localized Cu melting and resolidification reduces void content in W–Cu composites.
Transient complete melting of Cu around a W network minimizes phase separation during solidification.
Transient complete melting of Cu around a W network minimizes void formation during solidification.
Improved W–Cu interfacial contact enhances thermal conductivity.
Improved W–Cu interfacial contact enhances mechanical strength under irradiation.
Laser-fabricated W–Cu composites will have higher thermal conductivity than conventionally cast or sintered W–Cu composites.
Laser-fabricated W–Cu composites will have greater mechanical durability than conventionally cast or sintered W–Cu composites.
Vacuum-cast W–Cu composites tend to have higher porosity and less-uniform interfacial bonding than the proposed laser-fabricated material.
Spark-plasma-sintered W–Cu composites tend to have higher porosity and less-uniform interfacial bonding than the proposed laser-fabricated material.
Vapor-coated-and-sintered W–Cu composites tend to have higher porosity and less-uniform interfacial bonding than the proposed laser-fabricated material.
The proposed process is applicable to W–Cu fusion-reactor joints exposed to high thermal flux and irradiation.
The long-term high-dose irradiation behavior of the proposed laser-fabricated W–Cu composite has not been established.
